deep.reconstruction:
The page has two blocks, separated by a horizontal rule.

BLOCK 1: duality and the actions on M-valued presheaves.
Work over a commutative ring k with k-additive (k-linear, additive) categories. P is a small k-additive category, Q = P^∨ is its 'dual' (in practice P^op), and M is a k-additive target category.
- First line: Hom^!_k(Q^&; M) ≃ Hom_{k!}(P^&, M), 'si M k-add. stable par les deux types de limites'. Here P^& and Q^& are completions of P and Q, probably free completions under inductive and projective limits (ind- or presheaf-type and pro-type). The decorations ! and k! mark functors that commute with the corresponding kind of limit.
- The two sides are named Q_M and P^M. The intended statement is that, for M complete and cocomplete, both are another model of the category P_M ≃ Hom_k(P°, M) of M-valued k-linear presheaves on P. This is the universal property of a free (co)completion.
- Q = P^∨ acts on P_M by (F, L') ↦ F *_k L'. This is the tensor or weighted colimit of F weighted by L', a pairing P_M × Q → M that extends to P^&_M × Q^&.
- P acts by (L, F) ↦ Hom_k(L, F). This is the cotensor or weighted limit, a pairing P × P_M → M that extends to P^& × P^&_M.
- Passing to opposite categories exchanges the two: (F *_k L')° ≃ Hom_k(L', F°) and Hom_k(L, F)° ≃ F° * L. The braces record the change of roles (P, M) ↔ (Q, M°). This is the standard fact that a weighted colimit in M is a weighted limit in M°.

The purpose is a symmetric formalism in which a k-additive category and its dual act on M-valued presheaves by colimit-type and limit-type operations. It looks like groundwork for an 'abelianization' (universal abelian envelope) of a k-additive category, made symmetric under passage to the opposite.

BLOCK 2: tensor product of k-additive categories.
For P, Q k-additive, Grothendieck defines P ⊗_k Q together with a k-biadditive functor P × Q → P ⊗_k Q. They are defined 2-universally by Hom_k(P ⊗_k Q, M) ≃ Bil_k(P, Q; M) for every k-additive M.
- Explicit construction: objects are finite formal sums ξ = ⊕_{i∈I} a_i ⊗_k b_i.
- Morphisms: Hom(ξ, ξ') = ∏_{I×J} Hom(a_i, a'_j) ⊗_k Hom(b_i, b'_j), i.e. matrices, with the evident composition.
- In modern terms this is the additive (finite-biproduct) envelope of the naive k-linear tensor product of k-linear categories.
- 'À retenir': (a) if P and Q are small, so is P ⊗_k Q; (b) Hom_{P⊗Q}(a⊗b, a'⊗b') ≅ Hom_P(a, a') ⊗_k Hom_Q(b, b').
- The page ends mid-sentence: 'On en conclut que le foncteur can … (pl. fid !)'. He is about to deduce full faithfulness of some canonical functor. Most plausibly this is the naive tensor product P ⊠ Q → P ⊗_k Q, or a comparison of P ⊗_k Q with a functor category or with a tensor product of completions. Such a step would be needed to compare the tensor product with the abelianizations or completions of block 1.
errors: The final sentence is unfinished. If 'le foncteur can' meant the biadditive functor P × Q → P ⊗_k Q, it is not fully faithful, since Hom(a,a') × Hom(b,b') is not Hom(a,a') ⊗ Hom(b,b'). Full faithfulness can only hold for the k-linear functor from the naive tensor category, or for a comparison functor between completions. The intended functor cannot be read off the page.

The exact meanings of P^&, Q^&, Hom^! and Hom_{k!} are not defined on this page. My reading of which completion is ind-type and which is pro-type is conjectural. With the wrong pairing of variance, the first isomorphism would identify presheaves with copresheaves, so the variance conventions must be fixed by the earlier (missing) page.
The product ∏_{I×J} is a finite product, hence a direct sum, which is correct for finite I, J. Composition, which is matrix multiplication, is not written down.

ideas.what: Free completion of a k-linear category under colimits or limits; continuous or cocontinuous functors into a complete and cocomplete M identified with M-valued presheaves
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of the free (co)completion; enriched Kan extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory, 1982); ind/pro-objects: Grothendieck SGA4
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exposé I (ind-objects, presheaf categories as free cocompletion), in the non-enriched setting

ideas.what: Action of P and P^∨ on M-valued presheaves by tensor F *_k L' and cotensor Hom_k(L, F), exchanged under passage to opposite categories
ideas.modern_name: Weighted colimits and limits (tensors and cotensors) in V-enriched categories, V = k-Mod; duality colim in M = lim in M^op

ideas.what: Tensor product of k-additive categories with 2-universal property Hom_k(P⊗Q, M) ≃ Bil_k(P,Q;M) and an explicit matrix construction
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product of k-linear additive categories (additive envelope of the enriched tensor product); precursor to the Deligne tensor product of abelian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Enriched tensor product: Eilenberg–Kelly 1966; additive version folklore; abelian version Deligne, 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990)

missed.claim: In an 'Abelianization' dossier of about 1982, Grothendieck sets up a 2-universal tensor product of k-additive categories via biadditive functors. He does this alongside a symmetric formalism of tensor/cotensor actions and op-duality, apparently aiming at the compatibility of abelian envelopes with tensor products. That is the theme of Deligne's 1990 tensor product of abelian categories and of later work on abelian envelopes (e.g. Coulembier, Etingof–Ostrik). The page itself contains only the standard additive construction, so this matters for the historical record rather than as a new result.
missed.quote: Soient P, Q k-additives, on définit P ⊗_k Q et P×Q → P⊗_k Q k-biadditive de façon 2-universelle : Hom_k(P⊗_k Q, M) ≃ Bil_k(P,Q;M)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck considered tensor products of k-linear categories in connection with abelianization years before Deligne's published treatment. Whether the rest of the dossier proves that abelianization commutes with ⊗_k would be worth checking.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard enriched category theory: weighted limits and colimits, op-duality, and the tensor product of additive categories with its universal property. The only mildly notable point is its placement in an early-1980s abelianization project, which may anticipate the Deligne tensor product theme. Nothing new is actually proved on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top right reads 'si M k-add. stable par les deux types de limites' (for 'lim' read 'limites').
Line 'Soit' is 'Soit P_M ≃ Hom_k(P°, M)'; a superscript on P is crossed out. Similarly the crossed-out superscript in 'P_M × Q → M', and P^#_M (or P^*_M) in 'P × P_M → M'.
The overbrace above 'P_M × Q → M' is labelled P^&_M × Q^&; the underbrace below 'P × P_M → M' is labelled P^& × P^&_M.
'On a (F *_k L')° ≃ Hom_k(L', F°)': a crossed-out symbol precedes Hom.
The braces labelled 'P, M' and 'Q, M°' are drawn under F *_k L' and Hom_k(L', F°) respectively.
The scribble before the horizontal rule is a crossed-out word; there is no content.
'Construction explicite par familles finies d'objets de P × Q'.
'k-biadditive' qualifies the functor P × Q → P ⊗_k Q.
Last line: 'On en conclut que le foncteur can (pl. fid !)' — 'can' is inserted above the line, and the sentence is unfinished.
The '5' at bottom left is the archive page number; '②' at top is Grothendieck's own sheet number.
